EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
29 New Hot Wheels to Start Hunting for Soon
94 photos
Photo: Lamley Group
For most of the years I have collected Hot Wheels, I was quick to open any new package I got. Now, I have a line-up of nine cool Ferraris waiting in a box inside my car for several days. I guess this is what happens when you order too many 1/64th-scale models.
That’s not what I wanted to talk about today, though. Before I dive into the main topic though, let me just say that I had completely forgotten Mattel had started using Treasure Hunt collectibles in the Monster Truck series too. Will Trash It All arrived in Mix 2 this year, and uses the same black and gold paint scheme as the other three models: Duck N' Roll (Mix 5), Gotta Go (Mix 8) and Helichopper (Mix 12).
The latter the only one here that isn’t Brendon Vetuskey’s casting, and it won’t be the last time you’ll hear about its designer (Kurnia Alim). You’ll also notice some photos of a few interesting Hot Wheels storage solution, plus a hint about what seems to be an upcoming F1 chase car inside of an 8-Pack. I’ve got an even better F1 racer saved for the end of this story, and you might like to know that it will be available quite soon.
Anyway, let’s have a look at some of the 2027 previews available after the 40th Annual Hot Wheels Collectors Convention in Los Angeles. I’ll only refer to the cars I haven’t already discussed in previous stories, which means you’ll spot more than just 29 collectibles in the photo gallery. The first one that surprised me was the new variation of Fraser Campbell’s Porsche 908-3. This new livery takes after Claude Haldi’s car from the ‘70s, and is sadly missing the Toblerone and Shell decals.
Things are just like that in the Mainline series. Pass’n Go gets a new golden variation and it’s slightly better than the latest Drop Tops release. The 1965 Honda RA272 isn’t all that different this time around, and it’s safe to say that I’m glad we have a driver inside. The '69 Ford Mustang Boss 302 is still one of my all-time favorite Hot Wheels castings, even though it’s just half a decade away from its 20th anniversary.
A new Morgan is coming! Photo: Lamley Group It’s stunning in green, and I don’t even mind the black wheels for once. I’m not as excited about the latest variation of Corvette Grand Sport Roadster, and it’s not often that I’m completely uninterested in one of Brendon Vetuskey’s projects. We haven’t seen a Mainline version of the '73 BMW 3.0 CSL Race Car since 2022, as it has shown up as either a Premium or Silver Series collectibles over the past few years.
With this new livery, I’m certain it will fly off the pegs the moment it arrives in toy stores worldwide. As crazy as this might sound, I’d rather have the 2018 Bentley Continental GT3 instead: isn’t it amazing in grey and orange? The 2026 Morgan Super Sport comes as a huge surprise, as it’s only the second Morgan in Mattel’s portfolio. I wasn’t a fan of the Super 3, bu the Super Sport is playing in a different league.
The Aerodisc wheels are a bonus at this point, whereas the Armeria Lilac paint job will be the highlight here. The light blue Pontiac GTO is new to the game, but I’d be lying if I said I can accurately identify which casting this is. There are quite a few of them out there and I’m not a Pontiac specialist either. The yellow R34 GT-R will be one of the hottest cars in 2027, and I’m under the impression I’ve discussed about it before.
The next Treasure Hunt is a Tooned model Photo: Lamley Group It’s certainly in a league of its own, and not just because of those six-spoke wheels. Ryu Asada’s Nissan Skyline RS (KDR30) had two variations in 2026, and hasn’t had a Mainline release since 2024. It had the 3-spoke wheels when it was a Mystery Model in 2025, and I honestly regret not buying the Boulevard variation when I had the chance. While I enjoy bright colors on cars, I have mixed feelings about this light blue finish.
It will certainly be a peg-warmer next to the Stingassic Six Dodge, as that’s the kind of livery that might keep collectors enthusiastic for a few more years. The new Viper SRT almost feels like a page out of Neon Speeders, and it reminds me that we’re getting a special version of the iconic American machine in the Red Line Club next year. I almost fell out of my chair when I spotted the Tooned Purple Passion.
Not only is the color combo brilliant, but this is also a Regular Treasure Hunt for 2027! We don’t usually see previews of TH models until the day someone in Asia is able to do an unboxing for the world to see what’s coming up. The fifth iteration of Drift Ender is heading to a mini-series called Circuit Breakers, hence the unusual look. You’ll spot a few more quirky original castings in the photo gallery: they’re not something I want in my collection.
The Rondres W-33 is an exception for me: Ronald Wong and Andres Andrieu collaborated on this project. It’s styled after an early 2000s supercar, and it reminds me of either the Saleen S7 or the Jaguar XJ220 (which is obviously older than that). It’s the kind of project that makes me think fantasy castings aren’t so bad after all. I imagine kids won’t even mind that sort of thing. If you’re a fan of “Then and Now”, you’ll love the two, red, Honda Civics.
Forget about purple Lamborghinis, look at the Ferrari! Photo: Lamley Group
An FL5 would have been nicer than the FK8 but it’s still a Premium exclusive for now with no signs of joining the basic series anytime soon. After the two variations for Lil Mad, you’ll catch a glimpse of another Super Treasure Hunt for 2027 .
I don’t even want to imagine how much eBay seller will be asking for it in a few months from now. A Camaro 5-Pack wasn’t on my bingo card for next year: seeing just four of them in this previous is one way to create some excitement for the final version of the set.
It’s shaping up to be one of the best 5-Packs next year regardless of what other collectible Mattel is currently keeping secret. There’s certainly no shortage of options, especially with two new Camaro castings on their way.
Moving on to the Ferrari part of the story, the 12Cilindri comes as no surprise. And while the Ferrari 308 GTS looks decent enough in white, the purple Dino might almost start a treasure hunt if you ask me.
Disney and F1 together? Photo: Mattel Creations It immediately reminded me of the purple Ferrari F50 Challenge from 2001, which makes me want to go out to my car in the blistering cold to check if I have any purple Ferraris in my new package, too.
With all that behind us now, here’s another Hot Wheels surprise I didn’t see coming: the Disney x Formula 1 collab! I’m not saying I’m itching to get one for my collection, but I imagine the more hardcore F1 fans will like a closer look.
You’ll get three sets of Pirelli tires in the package, a new livery, and all for just $25. It might feel surprisingly cheap for a Mattel Creations Collaboratory special release, until you remember there are no opening parts like you’d typically get in the RLC series.
Oh well, it goes live on the manufacturer’s website on November 19 , 2026 at 9 AM PT. Your guess is as good as mine when thinking about how it might perform. It’s a case of love it or hate it, especially after what I’ve seen with last year’s first edition release of Fraser Campbell’s RLC-only casting.
